title: Sequenced SLI Prober and Region Failover Journey
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a lightweight, sequence-aware SLI prober and visual 'journey' to validate token-level latency SLIs across regions and to rehearse graceful degradation when circuits trip. The prober will synthesize realistic request shapes (short, mid, long sequences; dense vs. sparse token distributions; KV-cache warm/cold) and drive controlled load against routes in multiple regions to exercise batching, admit logic, and failover orchestration.

Why: Current golden-signal dashboards surface aggregates (p95/p99) but we lack a reproducible synthetic harness that ties per-token latency artifacts to admit/fallback decisions and can run as a canary during rollouts. This work reduces regression risk for multi-region capacity changes, kernel selection tweaks, and admission heuristics.

Success criteria (MUST):
- Prober can run controlled experiments that vary sequence-length distribution and KV-cache state and emit per-token SLI traces to the telemetry pipeline.
- New dashboard panels showing token-by-position p50/p95/p99 heatmaps, admit-rate overlays, kv-hit correlation, and failover transition markers.
- A documented canary workflow that uses the prober to validate SLOs before promotion of region routing changes.

Deliverables:
1) sequenced-sli-prober service (lightweight Go binary + config) with scenario definitions and REST harness;
2) instrumentation changes to emit per-token SLI spans and an admit-event tag;
3) Grafana dashboard JSON with panels: position-heatmap, admit-rate & shed-rate timelines, region-fallback stepper, kv-hit slice;
4) canary runbook and a short demo notebook for on-call use.

Non-goals: end-to-end auto-remediation, changes to tenant billing, or altering production admission thresholds without separate rollout tickets.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Triage: scoped after weekly SRE sync. Decided to keep prober separate from synthetic harness used in perf experiments to reduce blast radius.

2025-02-16 - Design: opted for per-token SLI emitted as lightweight spans (one span per response with per-token timing array in attr) to avoid high cardinality of separate spans per token. Trade-off: somewhat more post-processing required in pipeline; benefit: simpler emit path and fewer thrift/ingest costs.

2025-02-17 - Decision: scenario YAML schema finalized (sequence_length, prefix_warm_pct, kv_cache_policy, tokens_per_second, priority_tag). Will reuse existing tenant creds and route markers for canary runs.

2025-02-19 - Blocker: telemetry schema needs a new tag admit_event and kv_hit_ratio field. Raised ENG-213999 to update ingestion flattening rules. Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/452

2025-02-20 - Implementation: prober prototype pushed to feature branch (gh: redwood-inference/sequenced-sli-prober PR #68). Initial smoke runs against staging routes completed: captured position 1..200 histograms.
2025-02-23 - Review feedback from observability: move heatmap binning to the pipeline stage to avoid expensive client-side aggregations; added sampling knobs to prober to reduce event volume.

2025-02-25 - Integration: wired admit_event into canary dashboard. Created draft Grafana panels and exported JSON (dashboard id draft-SEQ-001). Demo saved to shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/seq-sli-prober

2025-02-27 - Next: finish documentation/playbook, add unit tests for prober scenario parser, schedule a runbook walkthrough with SRE and platform PMs (owners: Ravi, Maya). Planned canary for region routing change on 2025-03-11 if prober passes.
